_comment_encoding: 12.3-inch NQ5 (Spartan-7 scan). Output is dimmer2048 (binary, 0x000-0x800), not the dimmer800 (BCD 0-800) the file name says: the Spartan-7 bitstream multiplies register 0x35 as plain binary, so BCD gave a staircase (same fix as the 14.6-inch configs, 2ab724d). The file keeps its name because micropanel links it by name. sweep_table calibrations/dimmer800_12_3_nq5.csv was measured through the binary path on 2026-10-14 (FPGA v0x5A, dynamic local dimming OFF = the fixed neutral profile: the nits of full white also depend on the profile boost).

local_dimming_profiles._comment: Day/night local dimming (pixelpipe-fpga docs/dynamic-local-dimming.md; 12.3-inch NQ5 from FPGA v0x59). The detected zone selects raw FPGA 0x1E page-0 registers: ld_alpha 0x31 (LD max/avg blend, 16 = baked default; higher = small content brighter, more halo), pc_tune 0x33 (pixel-compensation gain/64, 64 = 1.0x; from the FPGA's linear-domain PC (0x4C = 1, docs §19) it multiplies the restored light: 64 = the LD-off luminance of greys, 83 = +30 % for daylight readability, white unchanged), bl_boost 0x49 (low-APL boost on the LED gain, 64 = off, 90 = up to 1.4x; from FPGA v0x77-79 the linear-domain PC divides it out per frame (B_ref/B, docs §20): the boost adds backlight headroom, i.e. less pixel lift and fewer clipped highlights in dark zones at more LED power, not brightness; content brightness is pc_tune), led_gain 0x43, bl_rise 0x4A. A zone must hold min_dwell_sec before its profile is used; registers then ramp by transition_steps per 500 ms iteration (0 = at once: from FPGA v0x58 the FPGA glides boost and alpha itself; pc_tune still ramps here). static_profile is used when the user switches dynamic LD off (set_ld_dynamic). Night: no extra brightness for dark content. Outdoor: maximum readability. 12.3-inch NQ5 (review v7 N34 option 1, decided 2026-10-15; FPGA v0x77+ with the per-frame backlight ratio): the day profiles raise the LED gain 0x43 (indoor 180 = 1.4x, outdoor 205 = 1.6x; night and static 128 = 1.0x for the lowest halo). The FPGA divides the gain out of the pixel lift (ratio B_ref/B, B_ref = LD-off's B at the 0x7F80 cap), so greys stay at LD-off x pc_tune and only white/saturated content and the LED power rise: LD-on white goes from 0.62 to ~0.87 (indoor) / ~0.98 (outdoor) of LD-off, never above LD-off per zone or in the mean (the cap 0x7F80 must stay at the LD-off white word for this). It removes the within-zone clip of bright areas (codes above ~206 flat in a white zone at gain 1.0; kept at night by choice). pc_tune is 64 in the day profiles (was 83: with white restored the +30 % is no longer needed and would clip from ~227 again). bl_boost stays 64: under the ratio a boost is backlight headroom, not brightness. The nits table was swept at gain 128: day profiles read ~gain^0.96 brighter on white (see brightness_to_nits).
local_dimming_profiles._comment_nits_gain: The nits table (calibrations/dimmer800_12_3_nq5.csv) was swept at led_gain 128. Full white at gain g reads (g/128)^e brighter: measured 2026-10-15 (FPGA v0x79, i1) at gain 180 / 205 x GD 100 / 50 / 25 %: 1.365 / 1.520, 1.375 / 1.554, 1.405 / 1.597, i.e. e = 0.89 / 0.94 / 0.99 (not flat: LED efficiency at low current). 0.92 keeps the nits API within about +-3.5 % over GD 25-100 % in the day profiles (exact at gain 128).

thermal_compensation._comment: Only the temperature source is used here (no factor table): the thermal_limit below reads the backlight temperature from the display IOC (0x66, register 0x1002, int16 x 0.1 C).

thermal_limit._comment: Keeps the backlight at about start_c (proportional): limit = 100 - gain_percent_per_c x (T - start_c), floor min_percent, moved by at most step_percent per 10 s reading (1 %: each step is a 1 % brightness change; 1 % deadband on the target); T = mean of the last two plausible readings. LD boost off while T >= start_c, back below start_c - hysteresis_c. No reading = no limiting. Soak values are from the 14.6-inch direct (2026-10-14: ~58 C at the cap, tau ~15 min); not yet measured on the 12.3-inch. start_c is the owner's choice pending the panel's derating spec; choose it as (panel limit - expected residual): the closed loop settles (T_unlimited - start_c)/1.72 above start_c, the 50 % floor removes only ~4.5 C (review v3 §4). 12.3-inch NQ5 (review v4 N20): this IOC NTC rises only ~3 C at full backlight power (LD-off white, tau ~1.5 min + slow drift; 38 -> 41 C in a 22 C room), so it follows the board more than the LEDs; at 60 C the limiter only acts in a very hot environment. Set start_c from the panel rating / sensor placement.
